verdicts.reason: B splits inline parsing into small single-purpose try* functions with a flat matchAt dispatcher and separates block grouping from rendering, so adding or changing a rule touches one obvious place, whereas A's renderInline is one long loop of nested conditionals with duplicated advance/continue logic; B's only wart is heading blocks using `text` while others use `lines`.

A splits inline parsing into small single-purpose functions (tryCode, tryWrapped, tryLink, matchAt) with an explicit nesting-level rule, so adding or changing a rule is a local edit, whereas B's single long renderInline loop with nested ifs and the inline block-grouping in render spread the same logic across more state to track.
